**THE OWNER'S THREE REVIEWS — the chair's thoughts, each claim measured against the code as it stands (master `a07ee4e0a`; the landing branch where named).**

Where the reviews are right, and already the program's direction: keep the deterministic, dependency-ordered pipeline and make its contracts explicit; validate MEANING, not shape; spend the next effort on coherence rather than breadth. That is what the audit (§934.101), the coherence window (§934.104), the soak ladder and the pool census have been doing since October: the ladder's STOP rule is a semantic gate, and the census makes every prose line declare the facts it presumes so the draw refuses a line the record denies — the reviewer's "independent semantic validation", built. The reviews read a snapshot five weeks and some fourteen hundred commits behind the tree; several of their findings are cured, several are confirmed, and the confirmed ones were slotted the same turn (the intake rule).

1. **Service providers (sewage system → food, lodging, entertainment; massive prison → trials and notary; water source → stabling; grazing land and farmland → milling). CONFIRMED IN THE RECORD, DISPLAY-CURED, MECHANISM MIS-DIAGNOSED.** The reviewer blamed the token-overlap fuzzy match. Measured over the 518 rows of the institution catalogue: 472 resolve by an exact service entry, 24 by the locale table, 17 by the fuzzy match (every one sensible: Mine → Mine (open cast), Caravanserai → Caravan masters' exchange, Sawmill (commercial) → Sawmill, Palisade → Palisade or earthworks), 5 to nothing. The wrong providers all come from one data table, `servicesData.js :: PROXY_SERVICE_HOSTS` — thirteen infrastructure rows "surfacing basic hospitality through the nearest service-bearing proxy": Water source, Multiple water sources and the three Dwellings rows → Inn/Tavern; Sewage system and the two Housing rows → Inn/Tavern District; Massive prison → Courthouse; Farmland, Common grazing land and Access to external mill → Mill. The chair's ruling RS-19 of 2026-10-30 already makes every display (the Services and Institutions tabs, the PDF, search) print NO provider for a proxy-surfaced service; the record and the JSON export the reviewer read still carry the proxy's name. **FIX-PUBLIC-VEIL'S STOP ON THE OPAQUE ID, RULED (2026-11-08, 01:36 UTC).** Measured first: inside the dossier JSON the NPC-id references are enumerable (npcs[].id; relationships[].from/.to/.id — the tie id embeds its endpoints; the crisis cast's roles[].id and levers[].holderId, in both stress containers), but ids are ALSO keys outside the JSON: `get_gallery_dossier` (migration 147) returns `gallery_member_overrides` raw to anon, keyed by the original NPC id, with `$veil` deltas addressing `card:npc:<id>` and `field:npc:<id>:<eye>`, joined client-side by id — so a sanitizer-only rewrite would leave the original ids public in the overrides and BREAK the joins (a field the DM hid would render: a new leak). Three options: (A) rewrite in the projection and re-key four server functions; (B) re-key at BIRTH — a veiled house's face id minted as `npc_veiled_<sha256(_seed | slug) prefix>`, the seam and `other` mints likewise for a hidden power's face, every join intact by construction; (C) leave it. RULED (B): one source at birth by the same predicate module; the existing id-uniqueness guard; no projection rewrite; the public-safe walk proves the house slug appears nowhere in the sanitized 525 and 1,000 and a tie still resolves; the goldens move under the lane's one unsigned cause; the edit layer never re-mints (a stable identity — a card moved into a hidden house by a DM keeps its birth id, an accepted edge); pre-car saved towns keep their old ids until regenerated (not the car's regression); `_seed` the salt. **THE OWNER'S WORD ON HOW THE SETTLEMENT DECIDES (2026-11-08, read at 20:38 UTC, the message minutes before, verbatim): "But these sorts of changes anything that deals with the whole settlement ultimately has to come from the head of the settlement, who goes and who receives sets off the floor and cieling for votes, complicated by risk, experience, reputation, relationship, current circumstances, and forward thinking, that then goes to a nationwide vote where the head power and those NPCS that make up the head power cast their vote scaling with their rank within the power, and that is also compared against the votes of all the other powers abd their members. It’s getting all complex, so why don’t you decide the best legal voting nationwide system? I think that it also has to reflect the government types in structure as well too each giving different weights based on states and domains. An autocracy for example might just make decisions solely based on the head and or nobles, a democracy might have each power’s member votes on an action and the majority based on votes per power wins regardless of power ranking, or other structures."** MEASURED: the engine has a GOVERNING POWER (`src/domain/rulingPower.js :: governingFactionOf`, labels by tier through `governmentLabelFor`), eight GOVERNMENT_PREFERENCES (council_rule, merchant_charter, military_order, temple_authority, noble_patronage, communal_assembly, criminal_shadow_rule, arcane_magocracy), five RULING_POWER_CAUSES (coup, election, succession, conquest, appointment), a persisted LEGITIMACY stock 0–100 with bands and a govMultiplier, the commons' unrest as a rung ladder (petition → gathering → riot), FACTION_POWER_BASES per archetype, and the court's risk appetite (`strategicPosture.js :: courtRiskAppetiteOf`, `courtPostureOf`); no stored government form. DECIDED by the chair as THE CHAMBER LAW (the owner delegated the decision; vetoable by a word) — ONE engine, FIVE forms, FOUR dials: (1) THE MOTION: the head of the settlement (the governing power's rank-1 face; the capturer's agent when the hall is captured) frames every settlement-wide question with a FLOOR and a CEILING — the bounded options — moved by six reads, each a receipt: risk (`courtRiskAppetiteOf`), experience (the head's practice in the office), reputation (the legitimacy band and the head's renown), relationship (the standing's person grain toward the counterpart), circumstances (siege, famine, treasury, war), forward thinking (the head's temperament). (2) THE FORM is DERIVED, never stored — `formOf(settlement)` from the governing archetype, the preference and the regime's cause: AUTOCRACY (military_order; any regime born of coup or conquest; a lord without a council), ARISTOCRACY (noble_patronage, temple_authority, arcane_magocracy), CHARTER COUNCIL (council_rule, merchant_charter), ASSEMBLY (communal_assembly), SHADOW (criminal_shadow_rule — the front's public form runs, the count bent by leashed votes); a thorp or hamlet has no chamber. (3) THE FRANCHISE AND THE BALLOT: every form seats the governing power's ranked faces; aristocracy adds the allied powers' heads as advisory; council and assembly seat every PUBLIC power (the criminal power never sits openly, it votes through its leashed agents); each seated PERSON votes within the bounds by their own read — their power's domain interest, their allegiance (a leashed voter votes the patron's line, the receipt veiled), their temperament, their ties to the head, their practice in the office at stake; every vote a receipt. (4) THE COUNT by four dials per form — H the head's share, R rank steepness within a power, P standing weight across powers, C the commons' aggregate bloc voting by its mood (the unrest rung), never as persons; the decision = H × head + (1 − H) × chamber; DRAFT bands, registered later: AUTOCRACY H 0.9, R steep, no P, C 0; ARISTOCRACY H 0.5, R steep, P high, C 0; CHARTER COUNCIL H 0.2 (the casting vote), R moderate, P moderate, C 0.1; ASSEMBLY H 0.05, R flat, P none (one power one bloc, the majority of blocs regardless of standing — the owner's democracy), C one full bloc; SHADOW the public form's dials, bent. (5) STAKES TIERS, the commission law's own: tier 1 routine — the head's decree, no chamber; tier 2 settlement-wide (a general, a trade pact, an alliance) — the chamber; tier 3 existential (war, capitulation, vassalage) — the chamber with the commons seated in every form. (6) THE OUTCOME: the chamber picks within the bounds or REJECTS; on a rejection an autocrat or an aristocracy's head may DECREE at a legitimacy cost (the stock dips, cause-reseeded), a council's or assembly's motion FAILS; every decision carried against a power's bloc deposits GRIEVANCE on that power toward the head, priced by the competition and stress readers; a failed motion, like an unfilled commission, is the party's door. (7) THE DM decrees any outcome or casts any named person's vote by hand, on the receipt. (8) LEGIBILITY: the dossier writes the division. WHY THIS ONE: it reproduces the owner's two poles exactly (autocracy H 0.9 with the nobles advisory; democracy H near zero, flat ranks, one power one bloc) and every other form is a point between, so there is one engine to build, one derived reader for the form, four registered constants per form to tune, and every vote leaves a receipt the DM can play. PLACED through the four seats (the fold's law under exactly `THE CHAMBER LAW` with the owner row — CONSTITUTION; INTERIOR's legitimacy and ruling-three rows and GENERALS H1's court choice as a tier-2 motion — LARGE; the leashed vote and the shadow form in ES, the division as a travelling fact in INFORMATION — COMPROMISE; the party's lever and the DM's hand in PT, the party brief and EDITOR — PEOPLE). **THE OWNER'S QUESTION ON THE FREE ACCOUNT (2026-11-09, 02:2x UTC, verbatim): "So what are your thoughts now on how the free account experience will be?"** MEASURED before answering: the entitlement ladder (`src/config/entitlementLadder.js`) — every size free; the Library `TIER_FACTS.free.saveLimit` saves against unlimited; custom content, the living Realm and map chains Cartographer's; gallery viewing both; the engine "constitutional", never tier-gated ("Every tier runs the same simulation"); the export bundle $2.99 per settlement for the free tier as a durable re-download right (`dossierEntitlements.js`, migration 108) against included; the Surveyor per task on either plan; the downgrade retention three months (`RETENTION_MONTHS`). The dossier's premium seams: the DM-truth reveals (`includeGroundTruth = premium ∧ ¬playerView ∧ ¬publicDossier` in Rumors, Relationships, War, the houses and the watch), the Faith section (a free owner sees a generic teaser naming no god; premium with a deity the content; premium deity-free no tab), the Faith & War PDF chapter canon-only and premium-gated, the `campaign_state` variant premium; the free PDF's "Free preview. Forge your own at settlementforge.com" footer. THE CHAIR'S ANSWER, given in chat: the free experience is the forge at full depth with the hidden layer and time held back — the right shape; a free DM reads the whole generation and every correction of the style wave; what premium adds is secrets (who really runs the town, the rumours' truth, the ties' leverage, the hidden allegiances the train is adding) and time (the Realm), the right things to charge for. Its weak points: the SHARED views — the public gallery projection and the player view fall back to legacy prose and the player view redraws the state prose (B10, SW-B7 after the train) — a free DM's players are the product's second audience and today see its worst text; the free PDF's cover printing "Free preview" beside "FOUNDER EDITION" (B1(d), SW-B4); the new depth of the train mostly premium by design. Two things to watch: the free dossier must read as the town as it presents itself, complete in its own terms, never as a page with holes where premium would be; and the shared views must be as good as the owner's. Both are the wave's work before the deploy. No ruling; an assessment, the owner's to weigh.

What premium gates (`includeGroundTruth = premium ∧ ¬playerView ∧ ¬publicDossier` in Rumors, Relationships, War, the houses, the watch, the launch tones, and `premium ∨ elevated` in the map's panels) is the LIVING REALM's belief-against-truth layer — the per-rumour DM truth and the wizard news, the neighbours' mirror, the war picture's ground truth, counter-intelligence in the world state, treaty intent, belief divergence — all of it campaign and world-state reads that exist only after time advances, and the Realm itself is Cartographer's. **THE OWNER'S SECOND QUESTION ON THE FREE ACCOUNT — THE COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT (2026-11-09, the second half of the message that gave the word to re-cut the painting, read at 02:44 UTC, verbatim): "Now comprehensively and in your own independent thoughts, what do you expect or how do you expect regular users to perceive and respond to the free account experience fully holistically objectively?"** Nothing new was measured for this answer; it stands on the first free-account answer's measurements above (the entitlement ladder, the Library cap, the engine at parity, the $2.99 export right, the "Free preview" footer, the shared views' legacy prose) and on the owner's tier law. THE CHAIR'S ANSWER, given in chat and set down here whole (the chat's three headings rendered as bold run-in lines; otherwise verbatim). It was given as a PROJECTION from the measured surfaces and from how DMs use such tools, not as an observation — each claim plausible until the telemetry confirms it — with no ruling; the owner's to weigh:

**The verdict.** Regular users will find the free account generous to the point of surprise, and that generosity will cut both ways. They will perceive a town that is deeper and more coherent than anything they expected for free, and they will keep most of their frustration for the moment they try to change one word of it. The free experience will be judged on three things in this order: whether the first screen reads well in ten seconds, whether the hooks and people are usable at the table, and how it feels when they hit the edit lock and the save cap.

**The journey, step by step.**

| Step | What most regular users will perceive | How they will respond |
|---|---|---|
| Landing and the arrow header | Handmade, confident, unlike other generators. A minority will not read the painted words as navigation at first | Most click Forge within seconds because it needs no account |
| The first town, about ten seconds | A real place with a name, a ruler, a founding wound and a mood. "The place" paragraph will be the moment they decide to stay | They scroll, open two or three tabs, and form their opinion before reading a quarter of it |
| The NPCs and hooks | The most valued part. Named people with wants, secrets and a "Connection:" to a house, and hooks they can run tonight | They copy a hook and three names into their notes and go |
| The depth beneath | Impressive but more than a one-shot needs. Vocabulary like powers, canon, Tonight and Substrate asks for the coach | Skimmers pick five things and leave happy; the long-prep minority reads for an evening and becomes the people who recommend it |
| Trying to edit | The sharpest edge. "I cannot fix a name without paying" reads as being charged to correct the tool's own output | Some pay, some regenerate, some leave annoyed. If regenerating a section stays free, this softens a great deal |
| Saving the third town | A cap of three feels tight for a habit the product itself encourages, which is forging many and keeping the good ones | They delete, or they stop forging freely |
| Sharing with players | Today the shared view reads worse than the DM's own, with old prose and redrawn sentences | Trust drops at the table; this is the fix landing before the deploy |
| Export | A $2.99 one-off reads as fair. A small "Free preview" footer is accepted | Occasional purchases from DMs who want the paper |

**The edges and the delights.** Three edges will generate nearly all the complaints. The edit lock first, because every DM wants to make the town theirs and the lock arrives in their first ten minutes. The save cap second, because three is below the number of towns a curious person forges in one sitting, and your tier law did not name saves, so this is yours to settle. The shared views third, because a DM's players are the product's second audience and a weak player view undermines the DM in front of their table. The vocabulary is a smaller edge; the coach and the group tabs carry it.

The delights are coherence and plainness. Everything attaches to something: the hook names a person who exists, the economy matches the ground, the governance paragraph names the seat and the powers. After the style wave the prose will read as a careful writer's rather than a template's, and users will feel that without being able to say why. Determinism is a quiet delight too: the same town for everyone who holds the seed, which makes sharing honest. The stance that the generator is an engine and not a language model will land well with the large share of DMs who distrust AI-written content.

**What I would do with this.** Keep the free tier as full as it is. The upgrade reasons, time, editing, custom gods and goods, the map, are the right ones because they are about what the DM wants next rather than about withholding the town. Make regeneration of a section cheap or free if it is not already, so the edit lock has a pressure valve. Raise the save cap or decide consciously to keep it at three, knowing it is the second complaint. Land the shared-view fix before anyone shares a link, which the wave does. Then measure four things from launch: how many free accounts click where editing would be, how fast they hit the save cap, how many shared links are opened by players, and which tabs are actually opened per dossier. Those four numbers will tell you whether this projection held.

Two of its four counsels touch the owner's open questions, not the chair's: the free save cap of three (asked above; the chair recommends keeping it, and this answer names it the second complaint — both stand, the owner decides) and whether regenerating a section stays free under the tier law (editing post-generation is premium's by the owner's law; regeneration is not named in the law and is NOT ruled here — a question added to the owner's list). The shared-view fix is SW-B7's, already ordered before the deploy.

**THE OWNER'S TWO WORDS ON THE PARTY LINK (2026-11-09, read at 03:2x UTC, verbatim): "Also make sure that the private view/link for players doesn't have any of the vote and comment stuff that shows on the gallery since it's not for showing publicly and for voting. / Also make sure that the link persists as long as the settlement does and any changes to the settlement doesn't creat a new link just updates the old one."** MEASURED before ruling, in the code and the SQL. THE RENDER: a party link (`/gallery?slug=<unlisted_slug>`) resolves through `fetchPublicDossier` (`src/lib/gallery.js` :456–:480), whose unlisted branch fetches no votes, reactions or view bump and marks the result `unlisted: true` — but the page that renders it is the gallery's own `GalleryDetail.jsx`, which branches on nothing: it prints the vote button on an undefined count (:273), "undefined comments" (:283), the reaction chips (:305), the comment thread with its composer (:321), the share-to-social button, Import and "more by this creator" (:322). The only consumer of the `unlisted` flag is the gallery card's badge (`GalleryCard.jsx:120`). So the players' page today IS the gallery page with empty social chrome. THE LINK'S LIFE: `get_unlisted_dossier` (migration 168 :287) reads the LIVE row at read time — `s.data`, or the narrated `ai_data` when the owner chose it — sanitised on the way out, so every change to the settlement shows through the same link with no action (CONFIRMED in the SQL); the link ends with the row (the slug is a column of `settlements`) or by the owner's explicit `revoke` or `rotate`. The one violation: `share_settlement_unlisted` (:211) MINTS A FRESH SLUG ON EVERY CALL and forces `is_public = false` each time, so a second press of "Unlisted link" — a stale tab, a second device, a reload before the row reads back — kills the party link the players hold; `src/lib/saves.js` :418–:423 names the hazard and guards it on the client only ("whose 'Unlisted link' button re-mints a FRESH slug (share_settlement_unlisted always rotates), killing the party link already"). `publish_settlement` (105) touches neither `visibility` nor `unlisted_slug`, so listing the town in the gallery leaves the party link alive (CONFIRMED); the admin moderation path (171 :227) nulls it — moderation, outside the owner's sentence. A THIRD FINDING the owner did not ask for and must hear: THE PARTY LINK IGNORES THE DM'S VEIL. The gallery read (`get_gallery_dossier`, 147 :42–:45) applies `_gallery_apply_member_overrides` with the per-member reveals, the "Reveal DM content" switch and the veil's deltas, and the client applies `projectShareVeil(toPublicSafe(…, { full, memberOverrides }))` with the row's overrides (`sanitizeDossier`, gallery.js :808); the unlisted read applies `_gallery_sanitize_public_json` ALONE (168 :298–:309 — no overrides, no full mode, no veil) and the client's unlisted branch hands `sanitizeDossier` a row with no `gallery_member_overrides` and no `gallery_share_dm`, so the players get the DEFAULT strip only — the rows the DM chose to hide or reveal for them do not apply on the one link made for them. The chair's answer of 03:0x ("built as the owner describes") was right for the gallery copy and WRONG for the party link; corrected here and to the owner. RULED, as four owner's-word rows folded into SW-B7 PUBLIC-PLAYER-VIEWS (its files; after the train, before the deploy; vetoable by a word): (b) THE PLAYERS' PAGE carries no social chrome — no votes, comments, reactions, view count, share-to-social, Import (the import RPC refuses an unlisted row anyway, 048) or "more by this creator"; it keeps the title, the author's name, the dossier in the player view through the veil, and a quiet Report link (moderation covers unlisted rows, 171) — a `dossier.unlisted` branch in `GalleryDetail.jsx` or a `PartyLinkView.jsx` beside `PublicDossierView.jsx`, pinned by a render test; (c) THE LINK IS IDEMPOTENT — `share_settlement_unlisted` returns the EXISTING slug unchanged, with no side effect, when one exists; only `rotate_settlement_unlisted_slug` mints anew and only `revoke_settlement_unlisted` ends it; a migration (unapplied, last; the deploy step's list grows by it at the merge) with `tests/security/galleryUnlisted.pglite.test.js` re-keyed by cause and a new pin: share twice, one slug; publish, the slug stands; (d) THE VEIL REACHES THE PLAYERS — `get_unlisted_dossier` applies the same `_gallery_apply_member_overrides` with `gallery_share_dm`, the per-member overrides and the veil the gallery read applies, and returns `gallery_share_dm` and `gallery_member_overrides` so the client's unlisted branch runs `sanitizeDossier` exactly as the public branch does (defence in depth, the same twin); pinned: a planted veil hides the same rows on the party link as on the gallery copy; `shareDm` then drives `playerView` on the players' page as it does on the gallery's; (e) the UI copy around the unlisted button says what the link does — the same link for the settlement's life, the town's changes shown through it, Rotate for a new one — under the style law. **THE OWNER'S QUESTION ON THE BRAND (2026-11-09, read at 03:4x UTC, verbatim): "What do you think about our brand the bronze plaque Settlementforge with the seal and everything?"** LOOKED before answering: the plaque crop `public/brand/plaque.png` (the brass plate with scalloped ends and two rivets; the wordmark in a dark serif with the crimson wax seal standing in for the O of Forge; the seal's impression a triangle over a bar inside a ring), `public/brand/seal.png` at 256, `public/favicon-192.png`, `public/favicon-32.png` (the impression dissolves; the derivation's own legibility cut ships the rimmed disc at 16), `public/og-default.png` (the plaque on a dark band over parchment; "Living settlements for game masters"; the second line "Economies · factions · NPCs · history · simulated as a persistent world" — the retired word and machinery, set in `scripts/derive-brand-marks.mjs` and re-derived only by the owner's Mac mint), and the header composite of 03:37. THE CHAIR'S ANSWER, given in chat, verbatim (an opinion, the owner's to weigh; no ruling):

I like it, and I think it is one of the product's real assets. My reasons, then the four things I would change, in order.

**What works.** It is a physical object, not a logo. In a category full of dark flat interfaces, sans-serif wordmarks and glowing dice, a painted arrow bound with crimson cord, a brass plate and a wax seal reads as handmade and sure of itself. People will remember "the arrow site with the seal". The seal standing in for the O of Forge is the one idea that turns the wordmark into a mark: it gives you a colour, a favicon that is honestly the brand, and a motif the product can reuse wherever it stamps something as canon. And it is a system. The bindings as navigation, the sign-in plate, the parchment, the serif on the share card, the PDF's seal all belong to one world. The share card's tagline, "Living settlements for game masters", is plain and strong.

**What I would change.**
1. **The impression inside the seal.** The triangle over a bar reads as a geometric glyph at 192 px and dissolves at 32 and 16, which the derivation script already concedes by shipping a plain crimson disc as the favicon. A seal needs an emblem that survives small sizes: a simple bold sigil, a monogram, an anvil or tower silhouette. That emblem would also give you the one-colour mark the brand lacks today, for print, embroidery, partner logo rows and dark tabs. This is the highest-value fix and it is small.
2. **The painting's provenance, decided before launch.** The strip is AI-generated art, credited in its metadata. Two risks sit on that, both specific to this audience. Tabletop players include a loud segment hostile to AI art, and your strongest stance, an engine rather than a language model, is undercut if the first thing they see is an AI painting. And AI-generated images cannot be copyrighted in several jurisdictions, so the brand's hero image is not fully yours to defend. The remedy keeps the design: commission a human painter to re-paint the strip from this one as the brief, measured and re-cut once under your header law, with a credit line the community respects. Decide this knowingly either way.
3. **The share card's second line.** "Economies · factions · NPCs · history · simulated as a persistent world" prints the retired word and ends in machinery. Your own style law wants something like "their economies, powers, people and history, kept alive between sessions". It changes on the next mint on your Mac, so it costs nothing to carry with the seal fix.
4. **The name's pull against the imagery.** Forge is a crowded suffix among tabletop tools and it promises hammers and anvils, while the arrow, cord, plate and parchment say survey, record and dispatch. The imagery is the stronger of the two and it matches what the product is, a record of a place. I would keep the name and let the imagery lead; I would not add smithy motifs to reconcile them.

**Two smaller notes.** The bevels, rivets and specular brass are a rendered style that some design-literate eyes will read as dated, which is a reason to have the flat mark in reserve rather than a reason to change the painting. And the wordmark gets small on a 320 px phone, which is acceptable because the plate, not the letters, carries the recognition there.

This is my eye, one data point. The pre-launch moment is the cheapest time to fix the seal's emblem and settle the painting's provenance.

For the queue: the seal's emblem and the share card's second line change at the owner's next mint (the derive script is a mint input; linux cannot record it); the painting's provenance is the owner's decision; nothing dispatched.

**THE OWNER'S QUESTION ON ALL THE DESIGNS (2026-11-09, read at 04:0x UTC, verbatim): "So what do you think of all the designs now?"** THE CHAIR'S ANSWER, given in chat (an opinion, the owner's to weigh; no ruling), verbatim but for its lead sentence ("Here is my honest view, design by design, then the three things that cut across all of them. It is my judgment, not measurement."):

**The generator and the dossier.** This is the strongest thing you have, and it got markedly better this week. A town where the hook names a person who exists, the economy matches the ground, the governance paragraph names the seat and the powers, and the same seed prints the same sentence to everyone is rare. The style law turned template prose into something that reads as written. The weakness is density: it offers more than a one-shot needs, and it speaks in its own vocabulary. The coach carries that, but it is the thing a first-time user will feel.

**The people layer.** The hidden allegiances, the fronts, the handler ties, patronage derived rather than stored, and a public face that differs from the DM's truth: this is the product's intellectual heart, and the architecture is right. The cost is intricacy. The veil now has client and server twins, per-person overrides and a reserved key, and every reader must agree. It works, but every future feature must respect it or it leaks.

**The tier model.** It was accidental and is now coherent: seven premium things, parity otherwise, with your two conversion levers named in your own words, the save cap and the regeneration boundary. I argued against the cap and you decided. What I would say now is that the design is defensible because it is deliberate: a free user who loves a town has a reason to pay, and nothing is withheld from the town itself.

**The sharing model.** The design, the dossier minus the rows the DM chooses, out by a private link or the gallery, was right all along. The implementation lagged it, and we found that only because you asked. After the party-link rows land, the players' page will be the view the design always described.

**The brand and header.** I said my piece and you have decided. The painted arrow with the bindings as navigation is the most distinctive thing a user sees, and the centred plaque now reads as finished.

**The simulator.** The most ambitious part and the hardest to make legible. Time is a real premium value for long campaigns, but simulation output reads as machinery unless the style law reaches every receipt, which is what the re-run pulse audit is for. I have measured it least this session, so hold my view on it loosely.

**The architecture words.** Dissolving factions into powers with memberships, ranks and seats is the substantive move; the renaming is cosmetic beside it. It is what lets patronage be derived and allegiance be hidden.

**Three things that cut across.** (1) Weight against velocity: the registers, doors, goldens, walkers and the thousand-town referee are why twenty parallel seats did not break the tree; after launch that same ceremony will make small changes feel slow — keep it in full for generator surfaces and lighten it for copy and chrome. (2) The launch gap: the world map is the premium feature people will ask for first, and it ships after the deploy; with the "Available at launch" pills, the premium offer at launch is thinner than the law promises — a sequencing fact, not a flaw, but users will name it. (3) Honesty as the brand: an engine rather than a language model, the same town for everyone who holds the seed, a dossier that is a record — that stance is consistent across every design above, and it is the thing I would protect most.

**THE OWNER ON HIRED FORCE: WORTH WHAT THE SETTLEMENT CAN PAY (2026-11-12 00:29 UTC) (the chair).** THE OWNER, verbatim: "does defense also calculate a merecenary charter or adventure guild charter as supplements to a guard or military, replacing them to an appropriate but lesser degree that scales to the prosperity of that settlement? do you agree wit hthis thought? because in my mind if a village or town doesn't have an active guard but can hire mercenaries or adventurers if they have the cash, then that means something rather than not having a guard at all." WHAT THE SCORE DOES, read by the chair in `src/generators/defenseGenerator.js` at 2cbe72ca1 and measured on 420 births (seeds `hire-<tier>-<i>`, the browser's dials; scratchpad `critique/probe8.mjs`): the military score adds walls 30, a garrison 28, a militia 10, a watch 7, a mercenary force 14, an adventurers' charter hall 10; the monster score adds the charter hall 35, its largest single term; a healthy mercenary chain adds 4. ONE upkeep gate, 0.6 + 0.4 x (economic output / 50) capped at 1, multiplies every paid defence alike. So: YES, it is a supplement and it counts — a village with nothing scores military 20 (mostly Vulnerable or Undefended), with hired force only 41 (mostly Lightly Defended; 8 of 120 villages), with a watch or militia 62. A town always has a watch, so the case is a village's. AND NO on the owner's two finer points: it scales with wealth no more than a wall does (the gate read 0.81 to 0.91 in the hired-only villages, and the Poor ones scored above the Moderate), and nothing in the score or on the page says a force for hire stands in for a guard that is absent, or that it is on contract. THE CHAIR AGREES with the thought and says why: a wall stands unpaid and a militia turns out unpaid, but a company for hire is the one defence that is nothing at all without coin, so it should move with prosperity more than any other term, and it should read as what it is — slower than a standing guard and loyal to its pay. RULED under the owner's deferral: it is built in this wave, by the two-phase rule. Given to COHERENCE-AGREE-2 as a fourth item (the defence home is that lane's): a proposal first — the smallest rule from one home, the page's words as declared lines with twins, the scores and labels before and after by what stands and by prosperity, and proof that a town with no hired force does not move — then the chair's ruling, then the build, then the lane's independent review.

**THE OWNER: PROSPERITY SCALES EVERYTHING THAT MUST BE KEPT UP (2026-11-12 00:32 UTC) (the chair).** THE OWNER, verbatim, a few minutes after the word on hired force: "prosperity should also scale the rest inlcuding healing, magic, etc. everything is based on what can be stockpiled, refilled, rebuilt, etc." THE PRINCIPLE, as the chair reads it: what a settlement can keep up is bounded by its prosperity — whatever must be stockpiled, refilled, paid or rebuilt (forces for hire and on wages, the upkeep of works, healing, magic, other services, stores, recovery after a loss) is worth what the place can sustain; what costs nothing to keep (armed households, the lie of the land, a volunteer muster, a vocation) is not scaled. The hired force is its first case. WHAT EXISTS, by the chair's survey at 2cbe72ca1: the defence score already holds this rule in five gates by economic output (military 0.6 to 1.0, monster 0.7 to 1.0, internal 0.65 to 1.0, economic 0.45 to 1.0, disaster 0.55 to 1.0), each identity at a healthy economy and each sparing the unpaid base; the magical score is gated by magic's own standing, not by wealth. Nothing else reads wealth: the services with healing among them, the magic envelope's availability and cost, the stores, repair and recovery. And prosperity is itself derived from food and output, so the order of dependence matters. THE CHAIR AGREES, with two cautions it put into the charter: not everything costs coin, and the existing gates' distinction between the paid stack and the unpaid base is kept; and a service scales in its stock, its availability or its price, never by the healer vanishing from a poor village. RULED under the owner's deferral: COHERENCE-AGREE-2's fourth item is WIDENED to the proposal for the whole rule — the inventory of every capacity that costs something to keep; ONE home for what a place can keep up, with proof that nothing feeds back into what prosperity is derived from; the rule by family with its floor; the page's words; the distribution of every label family before and after on the corpus, and prosperity itself not moving; three towns in plain words. (F2) EYES THE DM SHUT ARE LOST TO A SPELLING: the server's card id differs from the client's for an event whose label is null, empty or zero, and for a number the database prints otherwise than JavaScript; the hidden field is sent AND DRAWN, because the new client takes a served page as already veiled. (F4) AN AMPLIFIER: the member keys that withhold the full view are never clamped on the server and cost about three quarters of a millisecond each; 3,000 keys take a read to 2.2 seconds and 50,000 to 40, where 210 reads the same rows in milliseconds; any signed-in owner can store them and every signed-out reader then spends the database's time. (F5) Two costs that grow as document times veil. (F6) THE HEAVIEST REAL READ IS OVER ONE SECOND ON A SECOND MACHINE: the lane's own probe re-run reads 1,088 ms where the lane read 864; the veil adds about 500 ms, an address being parsed about twelve times (24,757 parses a read), and no helper can be inlined. AGAINST THE CHAIR: its timing stop was any native read over one second, and the lane's 864 ms passed it by a margin a second machine erased. A bound that close is not met; the chair accepted a number measured once on one machine. RULED (each vetoable). F1: a snapshot share never serves the live row; the server's bound is set from the worst-case ratio of the two measures so that every copy the client admits passes, and a copy over it is refused, not replaced. F2: the server's card id equals the client's for every value a row can hold, PROVEN AS A CLASS by a differential test of the client's id function against the SQL one over thousands of generated cards of every JSON type and awkward number. F3: nothing storable makes a read raise, proven by a fuzz of arbitrary documents and veils through all four reads. F4 and F5: the work of a read is bounded by the document and the clamped veil; member keys clamped as the client clamps them and only for people the document holds; the two product costs made set-based; the review's scale rows as pins. F6: an address parsed once, the hot helpers made cheap, and a target of 1.3 times the same read at 210 on the native engine, run twice, with a stop and the profile if it is not reached. F7: the map serves what the member's own listing serves, executed. THE ROLLBACK becomes exact SQL in the file with a rehearsal test that runs it and compares definitions byte for byte. FOR THE DEPLOY STEP: a read-only block of SQL the owner runs on the hosted database BEFORE anything is applied, answering what the reviewer wanted known (the roles' time limits; the largest stored copy; the most member keys; the longest list of hidden addresses; the largest counts of houses and anonymous events; any numeric id), written and tested by the lane's second seat. **THE OWNER RULES THE PICK: A GATE IS A DISQUALIFIER, FIT IS A WEIGHT AND NEVER A WIN; AND THE CHAIR'S METHOD COMPARED WITH THE OWNER'S DESIGN (2026-11-12 18:59 UTC) (the chair).** (1) THE OWNER ASKED, verbatim: "Objectively and holistically how does this design compare to what you've been doing and what's already done?" THE CHAIR'S ANSWER, recorded as given: the owner's design is the better governing idea, and the chair's method was the same mechanism applied one fault at a time (find a fault, cure its cause, guard it). That method prevented nothing new (nine new patterns in forty-five merges; the median town at 7 then 9), had no measure of done beyond no fault found lately, and checked each change against its own claims while nothing checked the whole page until the owner doubted it. What is already built is about a fifth of the design by the measuring seat's counts (672 of 3,342 lines that use a registered word declare; 54 of about 300 pick sites go through the declared door; two of four roots; sixteen kinds of thing). The design does not cover a record that is wrong at the source, the share veil or repetition: the four lanes in flight and the pools lane do. Its own risk is sameness, paid in writing. CHANGED: the second wave is measured by the rule's COVERAGE, layer by layer (lines declared, pick sites through the door, page findings by vocabulary at zero), not by a list of twenty-five; every new lane is held to the rule. (2) THE OWNER THEN RULED THE PICK, verbatim: "Change 2 should be weighted not gaursbtedd because then you allow for increased chance of repition. For me, I have a preference of checking for disqualifiers rather than qualifiers." The owner is right on the first: a guaranteed win gives every town of one shape the same line. TAKEN AS THE DESIGN, written at the charter's foot: a gate is a disqualifier and speaks only of truth (a line is in its pool unless something about the town makes it false; nothing is required of a town for flavour; a line true in one band only may be written as that band and is checked as the disqualifier of the others); fit is a weight and never a win (a seeded weighted draw among the lines left, bounded, read afterwards by the repetition guard); and the walker is what makes a disqualifier safe, because a forgotten one fails open, so a line that uses a registered word must carry that word's disqualifier. The chair's "the most specific line wins" of record 289 is WITHDRAWN. What the owner's preference buys: wider pools than requirements would leave, so less of the sameness the chair named as the design's cost. The mapping seat's measures of pool depth and of the pick are restated to it (the top line's share per pool under a uniform draw against a weighted one, by the repetition guard's rows).

**A HAZARD FOUND AT THE VEIL LANE'S PUSH: TESTS THAT RUN GIT INSIDE A HOOK FROM A LINKED WORKTREE ACT ON THE REAL REPOSITORY (2026-11-13 01:16 UTC) (the chair).** THE VEIL'S FOURTH SEAT STOPPED AT ITS PUSH AND PUSHED NOTHING (local tip 7cc74d252; the remote still f07db8760, read by the chair itself, with no stray branch on it). Its three cures are built and proved locally: V3-1 (three pins red at f07db8760 and green after; migration 211 changed by 24 lines added and 3 removed), V3-2 (counted at none on the probe and cured with a pin), V3-5 (the words); the veil's pins 39 of 39, the rollback exact, the six-size probe at zero on 8,136 reads, the id differential 26,515 with none unequal; the owner's count before the push is section 9 of the read-only block (3 on the fixture). THE HAZARD. The lane's hook runs the whole check, and four suites failed with no test run (the soak register, the landing stage measure, the implementation packets and the implementation session). They run git in temporary folders. Git exports the repository's location to a hook; from a LINKED worktree that location is an absolute path, so those git commands acted on the real repository: they moved the seat's lane ref, created two branches, set the repository bare and wrote a fixture identity into its configuration. The seat restored the ref, the configuration and its worktree, and did not retry. It never bit before because earlier pushes through the whole check came from a main checkout, where the exported path is relative and lands in the temporary folder. It is the scratch-worktree rule of this chair (record 275) meeting a hook that runs tests: every lane under the fast lane rule runs no test in its hook and is not exposed, and THE CHAIR'S OWN FINAL PUSH, planned from a worktree through the whole check, would have been. RULED: the cause is the tests, and it is cured on the veil lane ahead of its push, so that it reaches the integration line with that lane's merge. Red first and never against the real repository (a throwaway repository named in the exported variables; the four suites shown to write into it); one helper that spawns fixture git with the repository-locating variables removed, used by every test that runs git outside the repository (about thirteen test files spawn git, by the chair's count on the line); a walker that reds a test spawning git without it; the two stray branches deleted once read as fixture commits; the ledger ref fetched (the chair's brief had left that out); and before the push the whole check by hand, then the refs and the local configuration snapshotted, the push made, and the two compared, with a STOP if anything moved. THE CHAIR'S FINAL ACTS gain a line: before the last push, the helper is on the tree, and the refs and the configuration are snapshotted and compared. What this risks: a test that runs git by another shape than the walker reads; the snapshot before and after each whole-check push is the net.

**THE OWNER RULES HOW DEFENSIBILITY IS MADE: A SUM OF ITS SUPPORTING CONTRIBUTIONS, NEVER A RATING SET FIRST; THE CHAIR'S ONE-BAND LAW AND ITS CLAMP ARE WITHDRAWN (2026-11-13 07:01 UTC) (the chair).** THE EXCHANGE. The chair told the owner that the upkeep lane's review had found three towns in famine falling two bands of readiness, against a law of the chair's that prosperity may cost a place one band at most, and that it had ruled the law made true by a clamp. The owner asked what was wrong with a poor, walled city in famine reading as merely defensible; the chair answered that the famine's own penalties already apply, that in those towns the famine itself caps the label and the label then cuts the gates, so one event strikes twice, and that the cap was the chair's rule and the owner's to change. THE OWNER THEN GAVE THE DESIGN, verbatim: "I want defensibility to be derived from all of the supporting contributions that prosperity sets teh scale too in some. all of those add up to a score that shows how defensible a place is, rather than we set a place as defensible and then make everything match to that rating". TAKEN AS THE DESIGN, and it overrules the chair. WITHDRAWN: the one-band law as a rule of the product; the ruling of record 313 that it be made true by a clamp against the identity; and the line on entries into the two top bands. Each of them fixed a rating first and bent the parts to it, which is the thing the owner refuses. They had been set as limits on how far a lane might move a town, and the clamp would have built one into the product. RULED IN THEIR PLACE, for the upkeep lane's fifth seat. (1) READINESS IS THE SUM OF NAMED CONTRIBUTIONS: what is built (walls, gates, towers), who stands (a garrison, a watch, a militia, a hired company), what sustains them (stores, healing, magic), and the ground itself. Each has one home, each can be shown on the page, and the parts add up to the score exactly, on every birth. (2) PROSPERITY SETS THE SCALE OF SOME OF THEM, each at its own place and once: what must be paid, fed, refilled or rebuilt scales with what the town can keep up; what already stands does not fall because the purse is thin. The table of which is which is written first and shown to the owner. (3) A CRISIS ACTS ON THE CONTRIBUTIONS IT TOUCHES, ONCE: a famine on the stores and on a force that must be fed; never a second multiplier on the total, and never a label capped by the crisis that then scales everything again. (4) NO CAP, NO FLOOR AND NO CLAMP on the total or on its band: the rating is what the parts add up to. (5) MEASURE FIRST, and show before building in: the present formula's terms, each classed as a contribution, a multiplier on the whole, or a penalty on the whole; the itemised form; how the ratings then fall across six sizes, forced crises and births the lane never tuned on; and a handful of towns with their parts written out, for the owner to read. (6) THE CHECK THAT REPLACES THE LAW: every change of band between base and tip is explained by a named contribution's change, and the Defense tab's words are drawn from the same parts and never from the rating alone. The review's other findings stand as ruled (a house's own service is never scaled; one measure for stores; the hired company's line reads the label). What this risks: many towns' ratings will move, and by more than a band where the parts say so; that is the design, and the owner sees the examples first.

**THE OWNER: THE FACTS LOAD THE DICE, FROM EVERY PART OF THE TOWN; LIKELIER, NEVER CERTAIN (2026-11-13 08:25 UTC) (the chair).** THE OWNER, verbatim, in five parts as they came: "one thing i will say is vthat with random rolls added as we have designed, taking the following as only a singular example: The walls are sound or weathered. The floor and cieling sharpen for example if the prosperity is high, and they have stone masons and quaries either imported or as local resrouces or institutions that the walls are more likely to be sound. if you catch my drift"; "it doesn't mean they are always sound, but it means its more likely"; "and if the military guard is high in influence"; "and if they are in a frontier area that requires defense"; "all i'm saying is everything should be holistic". TAKEN AS: the facts load the dice and do not fix the outcome, and they come from every part of the town. THE LAW, amending the named conditions ruled three records ago: (1) every condition of a house or a work has base odds; (2) facts from anywhere in the town move those odds, each by a named weight: the town's wealth; the trades, houses and materials that keep the thing up, whether worked here or bought in; the standing of those who answer for it; how far the place needs it (a frontier, a plagued country, a crisis in force); (3) NOTHING GUARANTEES A CONDITION: the odds are bounded, so the likeliest case is never certain and the unlikeliest never impossible; (4) THE ONLY HARD EXCLUSION IS TRUTH: a condition whose line the town makes false is out, by a disqualifier, as in the procedure for pools. The earlier rule that pay, the chain and the crisis decide which conditions are open is WITHDRAWN except in that sense; (5) ONE TABLE holds every nudge (the condition, the fact, its home, the weight), so that adding a nudge is adding a row and the owner may veto any row; (6) COUNT ONCE: a fact either adds its own part or loads the dice for that part's state, never both for the same claim. Where today's formula has a direct term for the state a condition now names (the masons' term on the walls), that term folds into the odds; each such case is listed and ruled before it is built; (7) ONE DIRECTION: the dice read only facts written before the thing they decide. The standing of the guard as the page shows it is a power's strength, which is computed after the rating, from legitimacy, so it cannot be read back. Its measure is what is known before: the martial will, the garrison's presence, and the military power's standing as born if that is written before defence; the seat establishes which; (8) the page states the condition and gives no cause for it in this release; (9) THE PROOF, on births the seat did not tune on: the rate of each condition against each fact that loads it moves the way the table says, and no rate reaches nought or one except by a disqualifier. The same law governs prosperity's draw when its form is ruled. THE FOLLOW-ON SEAT is briefed by the chair from this record and the three before it; the fifth seat's hand-back gives only the technical state, to spare its context for the form it is building. What this risks: a table of nudges is tuning, and tuning invites a builder to fit its own births, hence the proof on unseen ones; a condition can now print beside a fact that makes it unlikely (weathered walls in a rich town with masons), which is the owner's stated wish and must not be read as a fault by a reviewer; the masons' fixed points on the walls become a likelihood, so their mean effect on a rating falls a little.
